narration.text: God said that after the flood, to eight people standing on an empty, washed earth. But first the great door had to open, after more than a year shut inside in the dark.
And Noah went forth, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him:
His bare feet touched dry ground. Behind him every creature came out, into a washed and silent world. Sheep and goats, cattle and birds poured out across the hills.
And Noah builded an altar unto the Lord; and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
Before a tent, before a field, before anything else, he built an altar. The first thing he did on the new earth was worship.
and the Lord said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth;
Read that slowly. The flood had washed the earth, but it had not changed the human heart. And still God chose mercy. That is the wonder of this story.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.
Eight people and a whole empty world to fill. Then God made a promise, not only to Noah, but to every living thing.
And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
Then the grey clouds parted over the valley, and for the first time in the whole story, colour stretched from one side of the sky to the other.
I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
A bow, the kind a warrior hangs up on the wall of his tent when the battle is over, pointed away from the earth and up toward heaven.
And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.

The family stood together in the wet grass and looked up for a long time. Every rainbow since has carried that same promise, hanging in the sky after the storm, for every person who looks up and believes.
Most people think the rainbow reminds us. Read the verse again: God says He will look at it and remember.
Next rainbow you see, what will it remind you of? Tell me below.
The full story is in the long video. Part twelve tomorrow: The tower of Babel.
